entry.title: Breakaway RVA, October 29
entry.content:
From Breakaway RVA



Let’s ride! We’re doing a special, multi-starting point ride to the @thewaroncars event at @studiotwothree on Tuesday November 3. All routes leave @ 5pm and the north of the river routes will meet at the Oregon Hill Overlook to join up with @recess4eva for the final leg to Studio Two Three. The route leaving the Stone House at Forest Hill Park will go straight to Studio Two Three. Starting points: the VMFA; the Waldorf School; Jefferson Park; and the Stone House at Forest Hill Park.

entry.title: Breakaway RVA, October 24
entry.content:
From Breakaway RVA



Tragedies, death and dismemberment are sadly part of history and in a historic city like Richmond there’s no shortage of the horrors which make for a creepy Halloween ride.
Join us Thursday, October 29 to learn some of the horrors of Richmond buried in the history of this city and please keep your eyes open for ghosts haunting these sites. The pace will be easy but we will climb the Franklin/Bank/9th Street hill. Please bring lights and a good blinkie light because much of this haunted ride will be in the dark.
Meeting time and location: 5:45pm at Clark Spring Elementary School (1101 Dance Street, Richmond, VA 23220
Meet at 5:45 and leave at 6:00pm
End Point: Clark Springs Elementary School

entry.title: Breakaway RVA, September 10
entry.content:
From Breakaway RVA



Join us for a follow up of this May’s Bridges Ride and explore Richmond’s Bridges NOT Over Water!
Join us for the story of 6 bridges, a lost expressway, and the most important Alfredo in Richmond’s history.
Please have your bike lights charged for this ride, as the sun is setting earlier and earlier!
5 stops, 13.5 miles, 1.5 hills. Post ride hang at Banditos.
Meet at Clark Springs Elementary school 1101
Dance street at 6:00 PM ready to ride at 6:15 PM.
What to bring: water, helmet, bike lights
Meeting time and location: 6:00 pm at Clark
Springs Elementary School
(1101 Dance St, Richmond, VA 23220)
Ride out: 6:15 pm
Post-ride hang: Bandito’s

entry.title: Breakaway RVA, August 14
entry.content:
From Breakaway RVA



Ever wonder how Richmonders moved around town in the year 1900? No, not cars, not buses. They walked, rode a horse, rode their newfangled “safety bicycle”, or they rode a streetcar.

Join us Thursday, August 20 to learn more about Richmond’s streetcar history and to re-create trips to Idlewood Park and Westhampton Park. This ride is approximately 13 miles (mostly flat) but with a couple impressive hills. Easy pace.

Meet at Clark Springs Elementary school 1101 Dance street at 6:00 PM ready to ride at 6:15 PM.

What to bring: water, helmet, bike lights

Meeting time and location: 6:00 pm at Clark Springs Elementary School
(1101 Dance St, Richmond, VA 23220)

Ride out: 6:15 pm
End point: Clark Springs Elementary School

entry.title: Breakaway RVA, July 14
entry.content:
From Breakaway RVA



Join us for a ride through the Revolutionary War in Richmond and discover the stories hidden in the streets we bike every day. We’ll visit the places where Patrick Henry inspired a revolution, Benedict Arnold invaded the city, and Virginia’s early government took shape. Whether you love history, biking, or both, this is a fun way to experience the city’s Revolutionary past!

The ride will start at Clark Springs Elementary, and the post ride hangout will be at City Dogs.

What to bring: water, helmet, bike lights

Meeting time and location: 6:00 pm at Clark Springs Elementary School

(1101 Dance St, Richmond, VA 23220)

Ride out: 6:15 pm
End point: Clark Springs Elementary School
Post ride hang: City Dogs
